title: Wild bets and PR
hired_for: To take bold swings without betting the business: every bet has a cap, stage checks and a stop rule, and PR, partnerships and events are judged by the traffic, links and orders they bring and what each order cost.

jobs.job: Cap what a bet can lose before it launches
jobs.why: A bold idea with no spending limit can eat a quarter's profit. The owner wants every bet to have a budget cap, a loss limit, a stop rule, a read date, a comparison group and a legal check before anything goes out.

watch.metric: share of live bets with all 8 limit fields filled in before launch

drives.metric: dollars lost on stopped bets versus their caps

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 live bets, 1 has a budget cap and none has a stop rule. After: nothing launches until all 8 fields are set; the worst case is $6,000 across all 3.

jobs.job: Stop a bet the day it breaks its own rule
jobs.why: Bets rarely fail loudly. They drift, and money keeps going out because stopping feels like admitting defeat. The owner wants the stop rule enforced on time.

watch.metric: bets past their stop rule or stage deadline, and dollars spent after the rule was crossed

drives.metric: bet spend as a share of profit after ads

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a pop-up series ran 7 weeks past its stop line and spent $11,000 more. After: bets stop within 3 days of crossing the line.

jobs.job: Keep total bet spend inside a set share of profit each quarter
jobs.why: Many small bets add up. The owner wants one quarterly cap across all bets, so no single month of experiments puts cash at risk.

watch.metric: total bet spend this quarter as a share of profit after ads
watch.source: brand brain (bet pipeline), Shopify, ad platforms

drives.metric: cash at quarter end versus plan

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: bets have taken 14% of quarterly profit with no cap. After: a 5% cap is set and the pipeline shows $8,200 of $12,000 used.

jobs.job: Get paid partnerships to bring orders at a cost we can live with
jobs.why: Partnerships and collabs often cost fees, product and time, then get judged on reach. The owner wants orders counted and cost per order set next to paid ads.

watch.metric: orders from the partner's code or tracked link, 30 days, and cost per order
watch.source: Shopify orders with discount codes, GA4 tracked links

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $5,000 collab is called a success on 400,000 impressions. After: it shows 62 orders at $81 each against $45 from paid social, so it is not renewed.

jobs.job: Give customers a real reason to tell a friend
jobs.why: A plain discount code rarely gets shared. The owner wants a referral offer people actually talk about, judged on the share of orders it brings.

watch.metric: share of orders from a referral code or link, monthly

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1.2% of orders come from referrals. After: a give-and-get offer with a status reward lifts it to 4% in 3 months.

jobs.job: Get ahead of a reputation problem with a statement ready
jobs.why: A bad post or product issue can spread in hours and hit sales for weeks. The owner wants a spike caught early and a holding statement drafted before it is needed.

watch.metric: hours from a negative mention spike to an approved holding statement
watch.source: brand brain (mention feed; proxy until a listening tool connects), review app, Gorgias

drives.metric: conversion rate in the 14 days after a spike

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a viral complaint went unanswered for 3 days. After: the spike is flagged when mentions pass 2 times normal, and a statement is approved in 4 hours.

jobs.job: Read each bet against a group that did not get it, then scale or stop
jobs.why: Buyers who got a bet may have bought anyway. The owner wants the gain measured against a comparable group left out, not against a good week.

watch.metric: gain on the bet's named metric versus the left-out group, at the read date
watch.source: Shopify orders and repeat rate by group, brand brain (bet pipeline)

drives.metric: added gross profit from bets that were scaled

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a founder video to top buyers is called a win on 40 replies. After: buyers who got it reorder at 31% versus 24% for those who did not, and it is scaled.

jobs.job: Swap a planned discount sale for a bet that protects margin
jobs.why: Deep sales train buyers to wait and cut profit. The owner wants to try a gift with purchase, a bundle or a price hold instead, and compare the profit.

watch.metric: profit after discounts during the sale window versus the same window last year

drives.metric: gross margin

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the fall sale runs at 30% off and gross margin drops to 41%. After: a gift with purchase holds margin at 56% with 90% of the orders.

jobs.job: Test demand with pre-orders or a small drop before buying stock
jobs.why: A new product or line bought in bulk on a hunch can tie up cash for a year. The owner wants real orders first, then a buy sized to them.

watch.metric: pre-orders or drop sales versus the target set before launch, in the window

drives.metric: cash tied up in slow stock

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3,000 units ordered on a guess, 1,100 sold in 6 months. After: a 2-week pre-order sells 640 against a 500 target and the buy is set at 1,500.

jobs.job: Scale a winning bet in steps, passing a check at each step
jobs.why: A bet that worked for 50 customers can break at 5,000, in cost or in team time. The owner wants growth in stages with a pass mark at each one.

watch.metric: gross profit per customer reached, at each stage

drives.metric: added gross profit from scaled bets

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a handwritten note program jumped from 50 to 2,000 buyers and the team fell behind. After: it grows 50, 200, 800 and holds $14 profit per buyer at each step.

jobs.job: Build a small inner circle of best customers who buy more and bring friends
jobs.why: The top few percent of buyers drive a large share of profit and word of mouth. The owner wants them treated as insiders and the effect measured.

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate of the inner circle versus similar buyers left out, 90 days

drives.metric: customer lifetime gross profit, 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: top buyers get the same emails as everyone. After: an invite-only group of 200 reorders at 38% versus 27% for a matched group.

jobs.job: Never miss a holiday, cultural moment or award that fits the brand
jobs.why: Good moments come every year and get missed because nobody started in time. The owner wants a dated list with a brief started 30 days out.

watch.metric: moments in the next 60 days with a brief started, and award deadlines missed

drives.metric: sales in moment windows versus a normal week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 of 5 moments this quarter had a plan. After: 5 of 5 have a brief 30 days out and 0 award deadlines are missed.

jobs.job: Get press that sends visitors and links, not just logos
jobs.why: A press mention that sends no visitors and no link is a nice logo for the site. The owner wants coverage judged on traffic, links and orders, and never counted as sales on its own.

watch.metric: visits from press coverage within 30 days, and new sites linking to us
watch.source: GA4 referral traffic, Search Console links report

drives.metric: organic search clicks and orders from those visits

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 placements last quarter, 0 tracked visits. After: 3 placements sent 2,900 visits, 11 new links and 46 orders.

jobs.job: Launch a delight bet only when service basics are sound
jobs.why: A surprise gift to a customer with an open complaint makes things worse. The owner wants reply time and complaints fixed first, and unhappy customers left out of the bet.

watch.metric: first reply time and open complaints before launch; customers with an open issue excluded from the bet

drives.metric: repeat purchase rate, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: first reply takes 30 hours and gifts go to everyone. After: reply time is under 8 hours before launch, and 120 customers with open issues are left out.

jobs.job: Screen a partner or ambassador before we sign
jobs.why: A partner with a bad past or a clash with our category can embarrass the brand for years. The owner wants a check done before any deal.

watch.metric: partners approved with an open reputation flag

drives.metric: reputation incidents tied to partners, per year

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 partners were signed with no check. After: every candidate is checked, and 1 of 6 is dropped over a category clash.

jobs.job: Turn an approved bet into a plan the team can run at its size
jobs.why: An exciting idea stalls when nobody knows who does what, by when, at what cost. The owner wants a short brief that fits the team's real hours.

watch.metric: days from bet approval to launch

drives.metric: bets reaching their read date, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 approved bets have sat for 6 weeks. After: each gets a 1-page plan and launches within 14 days.

jobs.job: Run one bet per customer group at a time, so we know what worked
jobs.why: When the same buyers get a gift, a mailer and a VIP invite in one month, nobody can tell which one worked. The owner wants groups kept apart.

watch.metric: customers in 2 or more live bets at once

drives.metric: share of bets with a readable result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 340 top buyers are in 3 bets at once. After: 0 overlap, and each bet reads clean.

jobs.job: Find the story a journalist would actually run
jobs.why: Most pitches are ads in disguise and get ignored. The owner wants 1 real story angle per quarter, tied to news, data or the founder's view.

watch.metric: reply rate on pitches, per story

drives.metric: press placements per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40 pitches, 1 reply. After: a data story from the brand's own sales gets 6 replies from 25 pitches and 2 placements.

jobs.job: Run events and pop-ups at a known cost per order
jobs.why: Events cost booth fees, stock, travel and team days. The owner wants orders and sign-ups counted with an event code, so the next event is chosen on cost per order.

watch.metric: orders and email sign-ups with the event code within 14 days, and cost per order
watch.source: Shopify orders with event codes, Klaviyo sign-ups by source

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $9,000 market stall is called great for awareness. After: it shows 110 orders and 600 sign-ups, $82 per order, against $45 from ads.

jobs.job: Keep a dated list of bold ideas, each naming the rule it breaks
jobs.why: Good bets come up in conversation and get lost. The owner wants one list with a date, an owner, a rough cost and the category habit each idea breaks.

watch.metric: ideas on the list with an owner, rough cost and named metric

drives.metric: bets launched per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: ideas live in 3 chat threads. After: 18 ideas on one list, 12 fully filled, 2 picked for next quarter.

jobs.job: Write down every bet's result, win or lose
jobs.why: Failed bets get forgotten and tried again. The owner wants a result and a one-line lesson on file for every closed bet.

watch.metric: closed bets with a result and a lesson on file

drives.metric: repeat of a failed bet, per year

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 9 past bets have a result on file. After: 9 of 9 do, and a failed mailer idea is caught before it runs again.

jobs.job: Run the ambassador program without it eating the founder's week
jobs.why: Ambassadors need tasks, content review and follow-up every week. The owner wants it run on a routine, with orders from each ambassador counted.

watch.metric: orders from ambassador codes per month, and posts waiting past the review deadline
watch.source: Shopify orders with ambassador codes, brand brain (ambassador list)

drives.metric: new customers from ambassadors per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 ambassadors, 14 posts waiting 2 weeks, orders not tracked. After: 0 posts past deadline, 85 orders a month counted by code.

jobs.job: Pitch the right 20 journalists, not a bought list of 2,000
jobs.why: Mass pitches get the brand marked as spam. The owner wants a short list per story, each writer checked for the right beat.

watch.metric: share of contacts on the list with a checked beat match for this story

drives.metric: reply rate on pitches

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a bought list of 1,800 contacts, 0.3% reply. After: 22 checked writers, 18% reply.

jobs.job: Put the founder where our customers already listen
jobs.why: Podcasts, reporter requests and awards can build trust at low cost, but only where buyers are listening. The owner wants appearances picked for fit and tracked.

watch.metric: founder appearances per quarter and visits from them, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain (appearance log), GA4 referral traffic

drives.metric: branded search clicks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 podcast a year, picked by chance. After: 4 a quarter on shows the buyers name in surveys, sending 700 visits.

jobs.job: Earn mentions that search engines and AI answers pick up
jobs.why: Buyers now ask AI tools what to buy. The owner wants the brand named and linked on the sites those answers draw from.

watch.metric: new sites mentioning or linking to the brand, per quarter
watch.source: Search Console links report; AI mention tracker as a proxy

drives.metric: visits from AI answer tools and organic search

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 mentions on the 10 review sites AI tools cite for the category. After: 4 of 10 name the brand within 2 quarters.
